newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes ease as storm concerns wane.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes ease as storm concerns wane.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes eased late on Thursday as concern over a Gulf of Mexico storm began to dissipate, traders said.
West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for August was trading around $19.90-20.00 a barrel in line with the NYMEX price, down from around $20.10 a barrel this morning.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was around WTI plus 23-27 cents a barrel, down from a high of plus 35 cents earlier.
The grade last traded at plus 25 and plus 26 cents.
WTI/Midland was at minus 23-21 cents, about steady with this morning, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was tighter at minus 26-23 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland was slightly weaker at minus $1.18-1.15, with $1.14 and $1.15 getting done.
Eugene Island was at minus $1.22-1.15 a barrel, with $1.125 changing hands.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus ranged from $1.93 to $2.03 over the course of the day, with the mid-range talked at day's end.
A number of Gulf of Mexico producers have shut in production and evacuated personnel in the face of a storm dubbed Danny. Two-day delays on the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP) were also expected.
